title: Richard Stallman, the GNU Manifesto, and Copyleft (1985)
explainer: In 1985 Richard Stallman published the GNU Manifesto to recruit help building a free, Unix-compatible operating system, and founded the Free Software Foundation that same year. The "copyleft" licensing idea worked out around then, culminating in the GNU General Public License in 1989, legally guarantees that redistributed or modified code stays open — which is why so many repositories a self-taught contributor reads today still carry a GPL or GPL-derived license and expect contributions to flow back under the same terms.
